question: A current of 0.4 A is maintained in a resistor of 2 Ω. The heat produced in the resistor in 1 second is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.32 J.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **formula to calculate heat produced in a resistor is H = I²RT,** where **I is the current**, **R is the resistance**, and **T is the time.**

 
 
• Current, I = 0.4 A
 
• Resistance, R = 2 Ω
 
• Time, T = 1 second
 
• Substituting the given values, **we get** H = (0.4)² * 2 * 1 = **0.32 J.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Resistance is a measure of the opposition to the flow of electric current in a material or component.
 
• Resistors are electronic components that are used to limit or control the flow of electric current in a circuit.
 
• When two resistors are connected in series, their equivalent resistance is given by the sum of their individual resistances, i.e., R1+R2.
 
• The equivalent resistance of two resistances R1 and R2 connected in parallel is given by R1R2/(R1+R2).
